signals.title: Red Sea shipping attacks divert oil cargoes around Africa
signals.body: EIA reported on June 11, 2024 that attacks near Yemen had prompted commercial operators to avoid the Bab el-Mandeb and Red Sea. Oil shipments taking the Cape of Good Hope route increased, adding travel time and cost.

signals.title: Bab el-Mandeb oil traffic falls as Red Sea attacks disrupt shipping
signals.body: EIA reported on October 11, 2024 that petroleum flows through Bab el-Mandeb averaged 4.0 million barrels a day through August 2024, versus 8.7 million in 2023. Attacks had led ships to take longer routes around Africa.

signals.title: Hormuz oil shipping continues during regional tensions
signals.body: On June 16, 2025 EIA reported that maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had not been blocked following regional tensions. Brent prices rose, showing concern about supply risk rather than confirmation of a closed passage.
